Philex Mining Corporation.desc: Philippine mining company, incorporated in 1955, that explores for and mines gold and copper. It has been listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange since 23 November 1956, and its principal office is in Mandaluyong City.

sources.title: Corporate Profile
Integrated Annual Corporate Governance Report 2023

Syrah Resources.desc: Mining company listed on the Australian Securities Exchange that mines natural graphite at the Balama operation in Cabo Delgado province, Mozambique, and runs an active anode material plant at Vidalia, Louisiana, in the United States. Revenue was US$33.4 million in 2025 and Balama produced 67,000 tonnes of natural graphite that year.

sources.title: Syrah Resources 2025 Annual Report (year ended 31 December 2025)

Petra Diamonds.desc: Diamond mining company with a premium listing on the main market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker PDL. It operates the Cullinan and Finsch mines in South Africa, with Koffiefontein on care and maintenance ahead of a possible sale, and the Williamson open pit in Tanzania; it sold 3.16 million carats of rough diamonds for revenue of US$367 million in the year to 30 June 2024.

sources.title: Audited Full Year 2024 results

South32.desc: Diversified mining and metals company formed in May 2015, with shares listed on the Australian, London and Johannesburg stock exchanges. It produces bauxite, alumina, aluminium, copper, zinc, lead, silver, nickel and manganese ore, and had 8,892 employees in the year to June 2025.

sources.title: South32 Annual Report 2025

Tozzi Green.desc: Italian company that works mainly in renewable energy, investing in hydroelectric dams and rural electrification, and in agribusiness. It began as a family business making electric control panels in a town near Ravenna after the Second World War and is based in northern Italy; revenue was nearly US$103 million in 2023, with operations in Italy, Peru and Madagascar.
Tozzi Green.note: No company filing or register entry could be opened. The nationality, base, business lines and revenue come from one reported feature (New Lines Magazine); the writer's earlier claim that the firm sits inside 'Tozzi Holding' and its 'Tozzi Renewable Energy' branch was not supported by any page opened and has been removed.

sources.title: The case against a carbon credit farm in Madagascar

Tiomin Resources.desc: Mineral company that traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange as TIO and held the Kwale titanium project in Kenya and a half interest in the Pukaqaqa copper-gold deposit in Peru, by 2010 reduced to payment and royalty agreements over both. Shareholders voted on 15 March 2010 to rename it Vaaldiam Mining Inc (TSX: VAA) on completing its acquisition of Vaaldiam Resources.

sources.title: MERGER: Tiomin to acquire Vaaldiam
Tiomin Resources Inc. Shareholders Approve Acquisition of Vaaldiam

Samherji.desc: Icelandic seafood company with its headquarters in Akureyri that fishes with seven vessels, processes whitefish at Dalvik and Akureyri, farms fish on land and sells through its sales and marketing arm Ice Fresh Seafood. Group revenue was 542 million euros in 2025 and it had 832 staff at the end of that year.

sources.title: Strong operations and solid finances at Samherji in 2025

Wildlife Works.desc: Company founded in 1997 by Mike Korchinsky that develops community-led forest conservation projects generating carbon credits under the REDD+ scheme. It has projects in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Colombia and Indonesia as well as Kenya.

sources.title: What We Do

Veolia Environnement.desc: Company incorporated in France, with its registered office in Paris and shares listed on Euronext Paris, that runs water, waste and energy services for cities and industry on five continents. Revenue was 44.7 billion euros in 2024 and it had about 215,000 staff.

sources.title: Multifaceted performance: Veolia exceeds all its 2024 targets
Veolia Environnement Form 20-F

Saipem.desc: Italian joint-stock company (Saipem S.p.A.) with its registered office in Milan and shares traded on Borsa Italiana, which does engineering and construction for energy and infrastructure projects through three divisions: asset-based services, offshore drilling and energy carriers. Revenue was 14.5 billion euros in 2024 and it had more than 30,000 employees worldwide.

sources.title: Saipem at a glance
Questions and Answers (shareholder information)

ČEZ Group.desc: Czech energy group that generates, distributes and sells electricity, with more than 33,000 direct employees and 3.5 million customers. Its shares are traded on the Prague and Warsaw stock exchanges, and the Czech Republic, through the Ministry of Finance, held 69.78 percent of its stated capital at 31 December 2025.

sources.title: About us
Structure of shareholders

Zijin Mining.desc: Chinese mining group incorporated on 6 September 2000 with the approval of the Fujian provincial government, with its registered address in Shanghang County, Fujian, that mines copper, gold, zinc, lithium, silver and molybdenum. It is listed in Hong Kong (02899) and Shanghai (601899), and in 2024 reported operating income of about 303.6 billion yuan, 1.07 million tonnes of mine-produced copper and 73 tonnes of mine-produced gold.

sources.title: Zijin Mining Group Annual Report 2024

Shanghai Electric Group.desc: Chinese maker of energy and industrial equipment, including nuclear, coal- and gas-fired, wind and energy storage equipment, elevators and electric motors, with its registered office in Changning District, Shanghai. Its shares are listed in Hong Kong (02727) and on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, its parent and ultimate holding company is the state-owned Shanghai Electric Holding Group, and 2024 revenue was 116.2 billion yuan.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Report
sources.publisher: Shanghai Electric Group Company Limited / HKEXnews

PowerChina.desc: Wholly state-owned Chinese engineering and construction group founded in September 2011 from merged power survey, design, engineering and equipment enterprises, including Sinohydro Corporation. It does planning, investigation, design, consulting, civil works and equipment installation for hydropower, thermal power, new energy and other infrastructure, and also works in real estate, investment and finance. A government-sourced profile gives revenue of US$42.4 billion in 2014 and about 200,000 employees and 1,565 overseas projects in 110 countries as at the end of June 2015.
PowerChina.note: The revenue of 645.6 billion yuan and 161,478 employees in the earlier version came from a market-data aggregator page for the listed arm (Shanghai 601669) and are not used; no filing for that figure could be opened.

sources.title: The Power Construction Corporation of China
sources.publisher: Belt and Road Portal (yidaiyilu.gov.cn), sourced from sasac.gov.cn

sources.title: Power Construction Corporation of China (PowerChina) - Directory of Central SOEs

Trans Adriatic Pipeline AG.desc: Pipeline company that owns and runs the 877 km Trans Adriatic Pipeline, which carries Azerbaijani gas from the Turkish border across northern Greece and Albania and under the Adriatic Sea to southern Italy. Commercial operations began on 15 November 2020, and by 15 November 2025 it had shipped more than 52 billion cubic metres of gas to Europe. Its shareholders are bp, SOCAR, Snam, Fluxys and Enagás with 20 percent each.

sources.title: TAP marks five years of safe and reliable operations

Tengizchevroil.desc: Kazakhstani partnership that operates the Tengiz oil field in western Kazakhstan. It is held by Chevron (50 percent), ExxonMobil (25 percent), the state company KazMunayGas (20 percent) and Lukoil (5 percent), and a third processing plant started producing in January 2025, intended to take field output to one million barrels of oil equivalent a day.

sources.title: Chevron Achieves First Oil at Future Growth Project in Kazakhstan

Union Development Group Co., Ltd. (UDG).desc: Company that the US Treasury describes as a Chinese state-owned entity acting for or on behalf of a PRC official. Treasury says it registered itself as a Cambodian-owned company headed by a Cambodian national and switched back to being Chinese-owned and operated within three years of receiving land; it was designated under US sanctions on 15 September 2020.
Union Development Group Co., Ltd. (UDG).note: 'Property developer' has been removed: Treasury describes the Dara Sakor project as ostensibly a tourism development but does not describe UDG's line of business.

sources.title: Treasury Sanctions Chinese State-Owned Entity for Its Role in Corrupt Practices in Cambodia

PT PLN.desc: Indonesia's state electricity company (PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara), which sells electricity nationwide and reports its results to a shareholders' meeting held at the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises. Revenue was 545.4 trillion rupiah in 2024, of which 353.17 trillion came from electricity sales, net profit was 17.76 trillion rupiah, and it sold 306.22 TWh.

sources.title: Pendapatan PLN meningkat 11,9% jadi Rp 545 triliun sepanjang tahun 2024

PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia (Lonsum).desc: Indonesian plantation company started in 1906 that grows and processes oil palm, rubber, cocoa and tea and sells oil palm seed. At 31 December 2024 it had 111,367 hectares of its own planted area and 12 palm oil mills in Sumatra and Kalimantan; it has been listed since 1996 on the exchanges that are now the Indonesia Stock Exchange, and Indofood Agri Resources became its majority shareholder in 2007 through PT Salim Ivomas Pratama.

sources.title: Company at a Glance
sources.publisher: PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk

SKS Microfinance.desc: Indian microfinance lender, formerly known as SKS Microfinance Limited and later renamed Bharat Financial Inclusion Limited, with 8.8 million microfinance customers. Its assets and liabilities passed to IndusInd Bank with effect from 4 July 2019, so it no longer exists as a separate company.

sources.title: Press release on the merger of Bharat Financial Inclusion Limited with IndusInd Bank
sources.publisher: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) filing

RATCH (Ratchaburi Electricity Generating.desc: Thai holding company in power generation and infrastructure, founded on 7 March 2000 under the name Ratchaburi Electricity Generating Holding Public Company Limited and now named RATCH Group Public Company Limited. It is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand as RATCH, its largest shareholder is the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand with 45 percent, and its equity-share generating capacity was 9,484 MW as of 1 April 2026.

sources.title: Company Background

WTK Holdings.desc: Group with timber, oil palm plantation and food businesses that holds eight timber concessions covering about 402,000 hectares in Sarawak, Malaysia. In the year to December 2024 its timber segment had revenue of RM203.9 million, its plantation segment RM295.3 million and its food segment RM103.7 million; its subsidiary Cairnfield Sdn Bhd stopped plywood making in Bintulu on 1 January 2025.

sources.title: WTK exits loss-making plywood manufacturing ops

Shin Yang Group.desc: Malaysian group with timber and shipping businesses and operations in Bintulu and Miri, Sarawak, described in 2010 as the largest player in downstream timber processing in Sarawak. In the year to 30 June 2009 it reported revenue of RM673.5 million and net profit of RM101.3 million; it had seven plywood mills in Bintulu and Miri and a fleet of 238 vessels through Shin Yang Shipping Corporation Berhad, which was then preparing a Bursa Malaysia listing for mid-2010.
Shin Yang Group.note: The earlier version said Shin Yang Shipping 'listed on Bursa Malaysia in 2010'; the source reports only that an IPO was planned for mid-2010, so the completion of the listing is not claimed here.

sources.title: Shin Yang likely to list its timber operations next

Proman.desc: Company headquartered in Switzerland that turns natural gas into chemicals and fertilisers - methanol, anhydrous ammonia, UAN and melamine - with plants in Trinidad and Tobago, the United States and Oman and a combined installed capacity of over 10 million tonnes a year of bulk chemicals. It also produces natural gas, builds plants and runs shipping and power businesses.
Proman.note: 'Privately held' has been removed: the company's own page describes the 'spirit' of a family-owned business but does not state its ownership.

sources.title: Who we are
What we do

WWF.desc: Network of separate conservation organisations that has worked since 1961 and has offices in more than 50 countries and work in over 100. Network services are provided by WWF-International, a secretariat near Geneva, Switzerland; the largest member, the US nonprofit World Wildlife Fund, Inc., a Delaware nonprofit corporation, had operating revenue of US$486 million in the year to 30 June 2024.

sources.title: World Wildlife Fund, Inc. Consolidated Financial Statements, year ended 30 June 2024

Twigg Exploration and Mining Limitada.desc: Mozambican graphite mining company that runs the Balama open-pit operation in Cabo Delgado province and is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Australian-listed Syrah Resources. A 2023 project record shows it approved for a loan of up to US$150 million from the US International Development Finance Corporation towards a US$175 million expansion to produce up to 350,000 tonnes of graphite a year.

sources.title: Twigg Exploration and Mining Ltda. (DFC-2023-TWIGGEXPLORATI)
Syrah Resources 2025 Annual Report (year ended 31 December 2025)

Société Minière de Dinguiraye (SMD).desc: Gold mining company that owns and operates the Lefa mine in Guinea and is a subsidiary of the gold producer Nordgold. Lefa accounted for over 20 percent of Nordgold's group production in 2018, when its mining convention was renewed; under Guinean law the Republic of Guinea was to receive 15 percent of SMD's share capital in two tranches within two years of ratification.
Société Minière de Dinguiraye (SMD).note: The tax and FODEL payment figures in the earlier version came from a paid advertorial on a news site and have been dropped; they are replaced with facts from a trade news report.

sources.title: Mining convention for Nordgold's Lefa mine renewed

PT Harapan Sawit Lestari (PT HSL).desc: Indonesian oil palm plantation and milling company at Manis Mata, Ketapang district, West Kalimantan, registered as a foreign investment (PMA) and listed as a subsidiary of Cargill Incorporated. Its land title covers about 5,137 hectares, and its filing describes a further 3,884 hectares of new planting, 1,200 hectares on its own estate and the rest with smallholders outside the title.

sources.title: Summary report of planning and management, PT Harapan Sawit Lestari

PT Permata Hijau Pasaman I.note: Blanked: no source opened names an entity with the "I" in the key. No source names an entity 'PT Permata Hijau Pasaman I'. An ISPO notice names estates 'Kebun Permata Hijau Pasaman unit 1' and 'unit 2' belonging to PT Permata Hijau Pasaman, which is the closest documented match; the description is of that company and its unit 1, and no separate legal entity is claimed. 'Singapore-listed' has been removed from the Wilmar reference as the filings do not state it.

Pengumuman Publik ISPO Resertifikasi PT Permata Hijau Pasaman

Wuzhishan L.S. Group.desc: Company recorded as Wuzhishan L.S Group Co., Ltd with an address on Street 55, Sangkat Chaktomouk, Khan Daun Penh, Phnom Penh. On 30 December 2005 it signed a 70-year Cambodian concession agreement for 10,000 hectares, within a 20,500-hectare area in O'rang and Sen Monorom districts of Mondulkiri, to plant pine, vegetables and fruit trees, tap pine resin, cut pine and build resin and wood processing factories.

sources.title: Contract for pine plantation between the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and Wuzhishan L.S Group Co., Ltd

Sabi Star / Max Mind Investments.desc: Max Mind Investments (Zimbabwe) Private Limited is a lithium mining company holding the Sabi Star project in Buhera district, Manicaland, an open pit over about 3,800 hectares with an estimated resource of about 5 million tonnes of lithium-tantalum ore. China's Chengxin Lithium Group, listed in Shenzhen, bought a 51 percent stake in November 2021 for about US$76.5 million.

sources.title: Sabi Star Lithium Mine
sources.publisher: Africa Mining Tracker, China Global South Project

PT Mikgro Metal Perdana (MMP).desc: Indonesian iron ore mining company, described as a joint venture between PT Allindo Indonesia and China's Aempire Resource Ltd, holding a production business permit over a 2,000-hectare concession on Bangka Island, North Minahasa, North Sulawesi. Indonesia's Supreme Court cancelled that permit in 2016.

sources.title: MEMR tells Mikgro to relocate iron ore mine in N. Sulawesi

Rui Feng (Cambodia) International Co. Lt.desc: Chinese sugar company in Cambodia, reported as part of a set of firms tied to Hengfu Group Sugar Industry Co., Ltd. of Guangdong province. Part of a 9,000-hectare economic land concession granted in Preah Vihear in 2011, later cut by 1,000 hectares, it built a US$360 million mill and refinery on a 215-hectare site in Chheb district that can process 20,000 tonnes of cane into 2,000 tonnes of refined sugar a day and employs about 1,000 people.

sources.title: Sugarcane in Preah Vihear (China in Cambodia special report)

Shanghai Xinmingyuan Automobile Parts Co.desc: Car parts manufacturer in Shanghai, China, which carried out lead-related production.
Shanghai Xinmingyuan Automobile Parts Co.note: Confirmed independently: the only page found naming this firm is the 2012 China Daily report on the Shanghai municipal government's findings, which describes it as an auto parts manufacturer and links it to the Kangqiao area of Pudong district but gives no address, ownership or size. No register entry, filing or company website exists that could be opened. Nothing beyond sector and city is claimed.

sources.title: 3 companies responsible for child lead poisoning

Shanghai Kangshuo Co Ltd.desc: Shanghai company that recycles used goods and materials, reported under the full name Shanghai Kangshuo Waste Recycling Co; it had relocated from its plant in the Kangqiao area of Pudong district by early 2012.
Shanghai Kangshuo Co Ltd.note: Confirmed independently: only the 2012 China Daily report on the Shanghai government's findings names this firm, and it gives no ownership or size. No register entry or company website was found.

sources.title: 3 companies responsible for child lead poisoning

Roads Department of Georgia.desc: Georgian government body that designs, builds, modernises, rehabilitates and maintains Georgia's roads of international and intrastate importance, keeps the register of those roads, checks compliance with road protection and use rules, and can temporarily suspend or restrict traffic in agreement with the Patrol Police Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Under the Law on Roads the Ministry of Infrastructure sets unified state road policy and hears appeals against the department's decisions.
Roads Department of Georgia.note: The Tbilisi street address and the ministry name 'Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure' in the earlier version came from a third-party organisation directory that was not relied on here; the law names the Ministry of Infrastructure.

sources.title: Law of Georgia on Roads (No 585, 11 November 1994), Articles 9, 17 and 22

Sakhalin Energy (Shell 55%, Mitsui 25%,.desc: Sakhalin Energy Investment Co., the company behind the Sakhalin-2 oil and gas project, including a liquefied natural gas plant with capacity of 9.6 million tonnes a year. Gazprom acquired 50 percent plus one share for US$7.45 billion in cash under a sale and purchase agreement with the shareholders, reported as done in April 2007, leaving Shell with about 27.5 percent, Mitsui 12.5 percent and Mitsubishi 10 percent.

sources.title: Gazprom acquires controlling stake in Sakhalin-2

PT Intraco Penta.desc: Indonesian supplier of heavy and construction equipment and supporting tools, which also does fabrication, infrastructure and power generation work and trades on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as INTA. Operating revenue was 954.68 billion rupiah in 2024, of which heavy and construction equipment made up 93.61 percent, with a net loss of 117.84 billion rupiah.
PT Intraco Penta.note: The founding year (given as 1970 in the earlier version) is dropped: the only sources found are aggregator and third-party profiles, and they disagree (one gives 10 May 1975). The 2025 revenue, loss and 496-employee figures came from a market-data aggregator and are not used.

sources.title: INTA Incar Peningkatan Penjualan Alat Berat pada 2025
Intraco Penta - Indonesian company profile

Sarawak Oil Palms.desc: Malaysian oil palm company set up in 1968, with its registered office in Miri, Sarawak, and listed on the main board of Bursa Malaysia as SOP (stock code 5126). It runs plantations and mills, refines, trades and markets palm products, and has a small property development arm.
Sarawak Oil Palms.note: The 7,513-employee figure came from a market-data aggregator and is dropped; the company's own 2025 annual report did not load, and the 2023 annual report's headcount sits in a part of the file that could not be read.

sources.title: Annual Report 2023

Yakjin.desc: South Korean garment manufacturer, headquartered in Seoul, which makes clothing for retailers including Gap, Walmart, Pink and American Eagle Outfitters and runs factories in Cambodia among other countries. The US investment firm Carlyle Group took a majority stake, reported as 70 percent, in December 2013.
Yakjin.note: The 1978 founding date and the count of eight factories (five in Vietnam, two in Cambodia, one in Indonesia) in the earlier version rested on a recruitment-site profile and are dropped; the facts kept come from a news report and a labour-monitoring factory record.

sources.title: Yakjin factory under review
Factory: Yakjin Garment

Vedan Enterprise Corp / Vedan Vietnam.desc: Vedan Enterprise Corporation is a Taiwanese food and seasoning company with its head office in Shalu District, Taichung; its predecessor Ve Cheng Food began making monosodium glutamate in 1954, and the company took its present name in 1972. A related company, Vedan International (Holdings) Limited, listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2003. Its Vietnamese arm, set up in 1991 with a factory in Dong Nai province, makes MSG, starch, glucose syrup, lysine and chlor-alkali, had 3,719 staff at its Vietnamese subsidiaries at the end of June 2024 and took US$79.5 million of revenue in Vietnam in the first half of 2024.

sources.title: History
MSG maker Vedan Vietnam earns $79.5 mln in H1, down 3.4%

Tunas Baru Lampung (TBLA).desc: Indonesian agribusiness owned by the Sungai Budi Group that makes vegetable cooking oil (Rose Brand), biodiesel and sugar, drawing on its own oil palm plantations in Lampung, and controls a land bank of more than 60,000 hectares. It has been listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as TBLA since 14 February 2000.
Tunas Baru Lampung (TBLA).note: The shareholdings of Budi Delta Swakarya (30.05 percent) and Sungai Budi (28.63 percent) are dropped: the only source for them is an undated third-party company profile.

Shell Brasil (Shell group).desc: Shell Brasil Petróleo Ltda, described by Shell as a subsidiary of Shell plc, which holds equity in Brazil's pre-salt offshore oil projects including the Atapu and Mero units.
Shell Brasil (Shell group).note: Confirmed independently: Shell's own release names Shell Brasil Petróleo Ltda as a Shell plc subsidiary with pre-salt interests in Atapu and Mero, and gives no stake percentages. No Shell Brasil revenue, employee or production figure was found on a page that could be opened.

sources.title: Shell grows interest in Atapu and Mero units offshore Brazil

PT Bio Inti Agrindo.desc: Indonesian oil palm plantation company in Merauke Regency, Papua, with land use rights over 34,195 hectares, 21,166 hectares planted as of December 2022, and three crude palm oil mills; it is POSCO International's palm plantation business in Indonesia. Daewoo International Corporation acquired 85 percent of it in 2011, when its concession was recorded as 32,500 hectares; POSCO held 60.3 percent of Daewoo as of 2013.

sources.title: Palm Oil Business in Indonesia (company response page)
Recommendation on exclusion of Daewoo International Corporation (27 March 2015)
sources.publisher: Council on Ethics for the Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global

Wintek.desc: Taiwanese touch panel maker based in Greater Taichung, with shares traded in Taipei, and a former Apple touch screen supplier. It lost NT$15.03 billion over the three years to 2013 and NT$3.42 billion in the first half of 2014, then from September 2014 shut a TFT-LCD plant at Yangmei in Taoyuan and three factories in China, laying off 2,360 staff in Taiwan out of an estimated 4,300 job cuts, and was expected to move into LED lighting and food biotechnology.

sources.title: Wintek says it is seeking funds, restructuring
Apple Touch Screen Supplier Wintek Restructures to Become New LED Player
Troubled Wintek to lay off all Taiwan employees

Thor Chemical Holdings / Guernica.desc: Thor SA ran a mercury recovery factory at Cato Ridge in KwaZulu-Natal, where several workers died after exposure to mercury fumes and sludges; the government closed the factory in 1991 and the Thor group then restructured through a demerger. Guernica Chemicals Limited is a South Africa-based company that the UK-based Tato Holdings group, described as the restructured former parent of Thor SA, approached in 2019 about the position at the Cato Ridge site.
Thor Chemical Holdings / Guernica.note: Confirmed independently: no source naming a company called 'Thor Chemical Holdings' could be opened, and the only parent named is Tato Holdings (UK); the entry therefore describes Thor SA and Guernica and claims nothing about a 'Thor Chemical Holdings'. The earlier claim that the factory took in mercury waste from chemical companies in South Africa and abroad is not in the page opened and has been removed. Businesslive and Companies House pages for related Thor entities were blocked or redirected.

sources.title: At long last, Thor's poisonous mercury is getting cleaned up

PowerChina Resources / Sinohydro.desc: Sinohydro Corporation Limited is a Chinese builder of dams and hydropower schemes, founded in the early 1950s, with its main office in Beijing and work also in other infrastructure and project financing. It was one of the enterprises merged in September 2011 to form the wholly state-owned Power Construction Corporation of China (PowerChina), of which it is described as a key brand and international flagship.
PowerChina Resources / Sinohydro.note: Confirmed independently: no source naming a separate entity called 'PowerChina Resources' could be opened, so nothing is said about it here. The figures in the earlier version (more than 10,000 employees, 524 international projects in over 74 countries, nearly US$42.5 billion of contracts) come from an unattributed, undated third-party directory profile and have been removed.

The Power Construction Corporation of China

sources.title: Power Construction Corporation of China (PowerChina) - Directory of Central SOEs

Rimbunan Hijau.desc: Malaysian family group founded in 1975 by Tiong Hiew King and his brothers, which grew out of hardware and construction materials. It works in timber, oil palm, hotels, retail, media, information technology and finance across Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Russia and China; the four dailies of its media arm Media Chinese International account for 70 percent of Malaysia's Chinese-language newspaper business, and Forbes ranked the Tiong family 25th richest in Malaysia with a net worth of US$820 million. Tiong Hiew King, the group's founder and executive chairman, died in November 2025.
Rimbunan Hijau.note: 'Who came from Sibu, Sarawak' is dropped: the source says Tiong was born in Sarawak but does not name Sibu or say where his brothers came from. The source gives no year for the Forbes figure.

sources.title: Sarawak timber tycoon Tiong Hiew King laid to rest

WTK Group.desc: Sarawak-based Malaysian group whose businesses span logging, oil palm, real estate and property development, manufacturing, hotels and shipping. Its main listed company is WTK Holdings Berhad, whose managing director is Dato Sri' Patrick Haw Yeong; his father Datuk Kie Yik Wong is a substantial shareholder, as is the apparently family-held WTK Realty Sdn Bhd. More than 30 companies registered in Papua New Guinea appeared linked to the group through shared directors and shareholders; companies in that cluster exported about 1.3 million cubic metres of logs between 2019 and 2021, around 14 percent of all PNG log exports in that period.
WTK Group.note: '12 concessions tied to it exported about 1.3 million cubic metres' is corrected: the source attributes the 1.3 million cubic metres to companies in the cluster, of which at least nine are logging companies and seven exported logs in 2019-2021.

sources.title: PNG's Timber Barons: #1 - The WTK Cluster
